body: Just to be clear, is this something you expect because you know your file has lint errors in it, but the wrong exit code is being sent along? (If your file had no errors, then I would definitely expect an exit code of zero)

Yes, the file has errors.

```
eslint file && echo $?
```

produces 1

```
cat file | eslint --stdin
echo $?
```

produces 0

Awesome. Appreciate the clarification- without the file and configuration, I had to be sure.

It does sound like a bug to me. Hopefully we can get this issue accepted quickly.

Pretty sure the commit was only done because we thought `process.exitCode = exitCode` was just cleaner/more efficient once we dropped older Node versions. If it needs to be reverted in order to get async stdin linting working again, I have no problem with that.
I don't think it needs reverting. It just needs the line process.exitCode = exitCode adding to the end of stdin callback

@shumphrey Thanks for the guidance.

In the same file, we have special handling for the `--init` flag. Assuming that callback is also asynchronous, should we also consider adding `process.exitCode = exitCode;` to the end of that callback? Thanks!
I think we can remove the local variable `exitCode`, then use `process.exitCode` directly.
I think @mysticatea is correct. Just have each of the three blocks set process.exitCode instead of exitCode

I confirmed.

```
$ echo var a | eslint --stdin --rule no-var:error --no-eslintrc --no-ignore && echo good!

<text>
  1:1  error  Unexpected var, use let or const instead  no-var

✖ 1 problem (1 error, 0 warnings)

good!

$ eslint test.js --rule no-var:error --no-eslintrc --no-ignore && echo good!

/path/to/test.js
  1:1  error  Unexpected var, use let or const instead  no-var

✖ 1 problem (1 error, 0 warnings)
```

issue.body: **What issue does this pull request address?** #6677 **What changes did you make? (Give an overview)** I removed the exitCode variable and made each block set process.exitCode directly. **Is there anything you'd like reviewers to focus on?** Confirm the exitCode is set correctly by running ``` echo var a | eslint --stdin --rule no-var:error --no-eslintrc --no-ignore && echo good! ``` should **not** get echoed after this patch is applied. Previously exitCode was set at the end of bin/eslint.js but the callback executed for --stdin was asynchronous. The asynchronous callback was setting exitCode after process.exitCode had already been assigned. This removes the exitCode variable and just gets each block to set process.exitCode directly.
